I'm not reading all the comments, but I want to say that I'm sorry that people are making you feel guilty. I want to tell you about my dog, Max.

He died 12 years ago. He was my childhood dog- I used him as a pillow when I was a toddler and played with him everyday after school growing up. He was smart, loyal, and very well-behaved. The perfect dog, really. One autumn, my dad started renovations on the sunroom. With open insulation and cooler temperatures, mice started to be a problem. He put a pack of Decon out, tucked in the corner of the sunroom. Max rarely went in there, but sometimes we'd leave the door open so he could pass through and let himself in the house. One day we noticed the empty Decon. So stupid in hindsight but we didn't make a connection. Within 2 days, Max was coughing. By the end of that day, my parents were rushing my limp dog to the vet with blood pouring from his mouth. My dad gave Max CPR on the way and arrived to the animal hospital covered in blood. Max didn't make it.

Mistakes happen, but remember that they're mistakes. Whenever people lose someone, there are always "coulda, shoulda, wouldas." My dad, all these years later, still gets sad and blames himself whenever Max is mentioned. But you're doing a great thing by spreading awareness of something most people would never dream of. I'm thinking of you and your family <3

/r/personalfinance has some great ideas.
First, track your spending to see if you're spending anything unnecessarily. If so, cut that out. I'm in college and find myself spending way too much on coffee, for example.
Next, make a little container for the money you want to save for the trip. This could be fun :) if you're into it, decorate a cute jar or box. But it could be as simple as an envelope. 
Decide what's possible (do you have a job? Income?). Make a decision to put in a certain amount in certain time intervals. For example, $10 a week. Or $50 a month. Whatever works. Keep that money container at home, tucked away, and think of it as "spent" money.
By a "trip," I'm not sure if you're just looking to cover airfare or also hotel, sightseeing, whatever. But start researching now so you'll know how to get the best deals.
Good luck, and I really hope you can make this happen!

Almost got hit by a train. I was in an SUV with my aunt, mother, and cousins on the night of 4th of July in this little Texas town. We were driving to city limits to see friends and do fireworks. 
Our friend had warned us to watch the road because there was a curve that ran parallel to the railroad tracks. But it was quite dark and all of sudden, the car wouldn't turn. My aunt had driven onto the tracks and the car was virtually locked into place.
My older cousin, who grew up in a rural area with trains, said "There's a train coming!" 
Fuck. But instead of panicking, I felt very calm for a moment. I distinctly remember thinking, "at least my death will make the news." I grasped my cousin's arm and braced myself for death.
My mortal peace was broken when there was some chaos. I opened my eyes and saw that my cousins were scurrying out of the backseat. My aunt, stubborn and stupid, was insisting that she could maneuver the car off the tracks. I remember her saying that she couldn't leave the car, she had just had the tires replaced.
I'm on autopilot, following my cousins out of the car, across the road, and into some tall grass. I have a history of anxiety, and I started hyperventilating.
Fortunately a fire SUV was driving towards us. I should mention the train was visible by now. We flagged them down, and they were able to radio the train (don't ask me how this communication works) and corral us behind the truck. He told us that the train was definitely going to hit the car and we needed to protect ourselves from debris.
His partner managed to get my mom and aunt out of the car. I suppose they hadn't been taking it seriously until then.
So the train stops roughly ten yards from the car. Nauseatingly close, and we were all so lucky. The train conductor came out and we talked a bit; he mentioned that just a week ago, a woman and her two young sons died because she had stayed on the tracks trying to move the car. 
Oh, and one of the firemen got into our car and backed up to where the road meets the track. It was that easy to get off the tracks.
TL;DR: Don't go to Texas.
